description: Behavioural evaluation set for the design-system skill. Cases pin token-only governance of an existing DESIGN.md, deliberate step-aside behavior when no file exists, extension drift, and atomic canonical-CLI routing. A missing, failed, or invalid declared designmd command blocks CLI-backed work with project-aware remediation; the skill never substitutes a reduced manual verdict.

evals.name: governs-existing-design-md
evals.prompt: Change the primary CTA colour to a warmer terracotta. There's a DESIGN.md at the project root.
evals.expected_output: Reads DESIGN.md first, updates the `colors:` token and Colors prose, cascades every `components:` entry that referenced the old colour, then runs `/design-system audit` (post-edit invariant) before propagating to code. Tokens come only from DESIGN.md — no arbitrary hex in components.

evals.name: steps-aside-without-design-md
evals.prompt: Restyle the hero section to feel more premium. The project has no DESIGN.md.
evals.expected_output: Does not block the edit or author a DESIGN.md from scratch. Recommends /award-design for a designed build — which authors the DESIGN.md up front and builds under it — and proceeds with a one-line pointer rather than forcing a file. init is named only as a minimal fallback when /award-design is unavailable.

evals.name: audits-existing-design-md
evals.prompt: Lint our DESIGN.md and tell me what's broken.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the audit subcommand and follows `references/subcommand-audit.md`: resolves the project-declared or installed Google CLI, validates its structured output, then reports broken-ref, contrast, and missing-section findings with concrete fix proposals. A missing or invalid CLI blocks with the exact project-aware install/repair command and rerun instruction; no reduced manual audit is presented as equivalent.

evals.name: migrates-legacy-stitch
evals.prompt: Our DESIGN.md is the old Stitch format with 9 numbered sections and no YAML. Port it.
evals.expected_output: Detects the legacy Stitch shape and routes to the migrate subcommand per `references/subcommand-migrate.md`. It resolves and validates the canonical CLI before mutation, ports the 9 numbered sections into the Google standard (YAML frontmatter + 8 ordered prose sections) atomically, then audits the result before handing it back. Any missing, failed, or invalid CLI result blocks without a partial rewrite and prints exact remediation plus the rerun instruction.

evals.name: audit-extensions-drift
evals.prompt: Check that our motion and shadow tokens match the globals.css @theme block.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the audit-extensions subcommand per `references/subcommand-audit-extensions.md`: checks bidirectional drift between the DESIGN.md extension namespaces, their prose references, and the globals.css `@theme` mirror — firing extension-missing-css, extension-orphan-css, and extension-broken-ref findings as appropriate.

evals.name: canonical-cli-integrity-and-yarn-pnp-resolution
evals.prompt: Audit and then migrate a legacy DESIGN.md in a Yarn Plug'n'Play workspace that declares @google/design.md. On the first attempt the declared binary cannot execute and yarn.lock is absent. After repairing the PnP environment, the CLI emits malformed JSON. After repairing the CLI output, rerun the migration and audit.
evals.expected_output: The declared Yarn PnP binary is authoritative and every missing/runtime/schema failure blocks atomically with exact remediation. Only a healthy canonical CLI may migrate and audit the file.
expectations: The resolver uses the project's Yarn PnP execution path with offline Corepack settings and never falls back to an unrelated PATH binary after a declared project command fails.

The first attempt stops before mutation, names the failing declared command, requires restoring or deliberately creating and reviewing yarn.lock, then uses Yarn's immutable install plus the exact rerun instruction; it never suggests yarn add for an already-declared dependency.
Malformed CLI JSON fails schema validation and stops without an audit verdict or partial migration.
The successful migration produces canonical YAML tokens plus the eight ordered prose sections and publishes the result only after validation.
The migrated file passes the canonical audit before the response considers the work complete.

evals.name: strict-audit-requires-award-design
evals.prompt: Run /design-system audit DESIGN.md --strict, but award-design is not installed.
evals.expected_output: Stops before presenting any standard or strict audit verdict. It states that `--strict` requires award-design, prints `skills add coroboros/agent-skills --skill award-design`, and tells the user to install it or drop `--strict`. It does not emit a degraded strict result.

evals.name: strict-audit-requires-both-catalogs
evals.prompt: Run /design-system audit DESIGN.md --strict when only anti-patterns.md is present in the award-design install and exemplars.md is missing.
evals.expected_output: Stops before presenting any standard or strict audit verdict, names exemplars.md as the missing catalog, and prints `skills add coroboros/agent-skills --skill award-design` with the alternatives to repair the install or drop `--strict`. It emits no partial strict result. The same hard stop applies when exemplars.md exists but anti-patterns.md is missing.
